name: Language-Table: A Large-Scale Visuomotor Robot Learning Dataset
description: Language-Table is a suite of human-collected datasets and a multi-task continuous control benchmark for open-vocabulary visuolinguomotor robot learning. Developed by Google Research, the benchmark centers on an xArm 2-DoF Cartesian manipulator moving blocks on a table surface equipped with a top-down camera. The release includes 442,226 real-robot demonstration episodes relabeled with free-form natural language instructions describing fine-grained continuous control goals, along with 181,020 simulated human episodes and 1,000,000 scripted oracle simulation episodes. It serves as a cornerstone dataset for language-conditioned imitation learning, real-time interactive language control, and multi-task robotic policy evaluation.

provenance.collection_method: Real-world teleoperation and autonomous playback using a Cartesian xArm manipulator with an overhead camera interacting with colored geometric blocks, paired with offline human crowd-sourced language relabeling.
provenance.curation_notes: Encompasses real-robot, human simulation, and scripted oracle simulation collections. Only the real-robot 442,226 episode subset is counted as primary real-world samples.
